source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A long-term informal career adviser who supports professional development but does not participate in clinical orientation or competency evaluation.","B":"An experienced clinician who provides structured role-specific orientation, coaching, feedback, and performance evaluation during transition into practice.","C":"A disciplinary manager whose primary function is enforcing attendance and employment rules rather than coaching transition into the clinical role.","D":"A peer selected for social support who does not observe clinical practice, evaluate performance, or provide role-specific feedback."}}
source_row.rationale: Open RN describes preceptors as experienced nurses who serve as role models and resources, coach the new nurse into the role, evaluate performance, and provide feedback during transition into practice.
source_row.source_detail: Chapter 11, Preparation for the RN Role > Transitioning Into Practice / preceptor role. Open RN 2nd edition, 2024; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A nurse educator explains the difference between a preceptor and a mentor. Which description best fits a preceptor?
